disclaimer: Verify current Ejari fees, RERA rent-increase slabs, and Rental Disputes Centre filing rules with the Dubai Land Department (DLD) before acting.

ejari.name: Ejari registration
ejari.summary: Ejari is the mandatory DLD system that registers a Dubai tenancy contract. An active Ejari is a precondition for DEWA activation, mainland visa quotas, and filing at the Rental Disputes Centre.
required_documents: Unified tenancy contract (copy for the app; original at a trustee centre)
Applicant Emirates ID when applying at a trustee centre
Official power of attorney when applying as a representative, subject to the issuing emirate requirements

fees_notes.dubai_rest_app: AED 100 registration + AED 10 knowledge + AED 10 innovation + AED 55 service partner fee + AED 2.75 VAT.
fees_notes.real_estate_trustee_centre: DLD publishes a rounded total of AED 220. Its listed components (100 + 10 + 10 + 95 + 5% VAT on 95) total AED 219.75; confirm the payable total at checkout.

timeline.dubai_rest_app: Certificate sent by email after review and approval; no separate app completion target stated on the service page.
timeline.trustee_centre: 25 minutes excluding waiting time, per the DLD service target.

common_mistakes: Not registering Ejari before applying for a mainland visa quota (Ejari is a precondition)
Using the wrong DEWA premise number
Trying to file at the Rental Disputes Centre or activate DEWA without an active Ejari

flexi_rent.name: DLD Flexi Rent initiative
flexi_rent.summary: The Dubai Land Department's Flexi Rent initiative lets tenants pay annual rent in monthly, quarterly, or semi-annual instalments through approved partner real estate firms, instead of the traditional 1-4 cheques.
how_it_works: Applies to new and renewed contracts with participating landlords
Rent payable in monthly, quarterly, or semi-annual instalments with no premium over the annual amount
Allows grace periods and waived bounced-cheque fees
In specific cases the annual rent increase can be waived
Existing tenants can request conversion via participating property managers
flexi_rent.note: This changes the standard 'rent in 1-4 cheques' guidance: instalment plans are now an official DLD option through approved partners.

rera_rent_increase.summary: The maximum allowed rent increase at renewal depends on how far the current rent sits below the area average market rent on the RERA Rent Index.

slabs.description: Current rent is up to 10% below the average rent: no increase allowed (0%).
Current rent is 11-20% below the area average: up to 5% increase.
Current rent is 21-30% below the area average: up to 10% increase.
Current rent is 31-40% below the area average: up to 15% increase.
Current rent is more than 40% below the area average: up to 20% increase.

rera_rent_increase.notice_rule: At least 90 days notice before expiry to change rent or contract terms, unless the parties agree otherwise.
rera_rent_increase.rent_cap_status: DLD guidance checked on 2026-09-05 retains the Decree 43 of 2013 bands. A gap of exactly 10% attracts no increase. Use the official Rental Index for the property and renewal date.

rdc.name: Rental Disputes Centre (part of DLD)
rdc.summary: The Rental Disputes Centre (RDC) handles landlord and tenant disputes in Dubai.
rdc.filing_fee: Two tracks. Non-monetary claims (eviction, renewal, rent recovery, termination): 3.5% of the annual rent or lease value, minimum AED 500, maximum AED 20,000. Monetary claims: 3.5% of the amount claimed, minimum AED 500, maximum AED 15,000.
rdc.filing_fee_note: The AED 20,000 and AED 15,000 figures are ceilings on the FILING FEE, not limits on what a party may claim. There is no cap on the value of a claim the RDC will hear. A monetary claim above about AED 428,571 simply plateaus at the AED 15,000 fee.
channels: in person at DLD HQ in Deira

additional_fees_aed.service_partner_note: AED 130 plus VAT if filed through a trustee office.

shared_housing.name: Shared housing / co-living regulation
shared_housing.in_force: Upcoming as of 2026-09-05: effective 2026-09-08, calculated as 180 days after Official Gazette publication on 2026-03-12.
shared_housing.summary: Law No. 4 of 2026 regulates the occupancy and management of shared housing (bed space, partitioned, and co-living arrangements) in Dubai: operator permits, an electronic Shared Housing Registry, minimum space per resident, and fines up to AED 1,000,000.
key_rules: No unit may be allocated to shared housing without a permit (valid 1 year, renewable)
DLD manages an electronic Shared Housing Registry linked to Dubai Municipality
Only property owners, licensed property-management firms, or licensed subleasing entities may operate shared housing; tenants cannot sublease
Dubai Municipality determines occupancy limits, minimum space and technical standards through implementing requirements; the Law itself does not specify a universal 5 sqm-per-resident minimum.

fines.repeat_violation_rule: Fines double for repeat violations within a year, up to a maximum of AED 1,000,000

shared_housing.grace_period: Existing operators have 1 year from commencement to comply (to 2027-09-08 on the stated commencement calculation); the Director General of Dubai Municipality may grant one extension.

dld_initiatives_2026.summary: One-line status of DLD initiatives relevant to Dubai tenants and buyers, as of 2026-07-02.
dld_initiatives_2026.first_time_home_buyer: First-Time Home Buyer programme (launched July 2025) expanded to 22 participating developers as of June 2026.
dld_initiatives_2026.tokenization: Real estate tokenization Phase 2 live since 2026-02-20, with a regulated (VARA-supervised) secondary market on PRYPCO Mint.
dld_initiatives_2026.smart_rental_index: Smart Rental Index benchmarks refreshed for 2026; building star ratings and the 90-day notice rule continue to apply.
